North Korean Hackers Account for Nearly 89% of Reported Crypto Theft Losses in 2026, South Korea Estimates Over 8,000 Related Personnel Chainalysis said that so far in 2026, suspected North Korea-linked hacks have accounted for nearly 89% of reported cryptocurrency hack losses, up from 15% in 2021. In addition, North Korean hackers are increasingly using generative AI to create fake documents and impersonate technical personnel. The South Korean government estimates that North Korean authorities deploy more than 8,000 related personnel. — link

Chainalysis: Names, Usernames, Password Hashes, and Valid Tokens of All Users Were Exposed; Some Plaintext Passwords Also Leaked Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis disclosed in an updated security incident notice that the names, usernames, password hashes, and valid authentication tokens of all users had been exposed to the attacker, and that some customers’ plaintext passwords were also leaked through a separate attack method. After detecting abnormal activity, the company suspended KYT transaction monitoring, address screening, and login services, and required all users to reset their passwords and rotate API keys where necessary. Previously, on October 30, Chainalysis first disclosed that it had been breached by a hacker using offensive AI agent technology; at that time it only confirmed that certain customer identity information had been accessed and said it had found no evidence that passwords or session tokens had been leaked. — link

Leading Crypto Critic Elizabeth Warren Expected to Become Chair of the U.S. Senate Banking Committee in January Next Year, with Focus Likely on Cryptocurrency Regulation According to The Wall Street Journal, Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren, a longtime advocate for stronger regulation of the crypto industry, is expected to become chair of the U.S. Senate Banking Committee in January next year, gaining broader oversight of the financial industry and subpoena powers. The report noted that her early priorities may include investigating alleged insider trading in prediction markets, reviewing consumer protection practices of cryptocurrency firms, and examining alleged conflicts of interest involving Trump and his family members. Warren’s appointment as chair has not yet been finalized, but most Senate observers believe the likelihood of a competing candidate is low. — link

Democrats Take Control of the House; World Liberty Financial Likely Among First Investigation Targets, Trump’s Pardon of Zhao Changpeng Also to Be Reviewed Democrats have won control of the U.S. House of Representatives. Representative Robert Garcia, who is expected to chair the House Oversight Committee, said the committee will investigate the Trump family’s business dealings, including its cryptocurrency ventures. The family’s related company, World Liberty Financial, is likely to be among the first investigation targets, with related inquiries possibly starting as early as February. Democrats also said they will investigate Trump’s pardon of Binance co-founder Zhao Changpeng, who previously helped the Trump family launch a stablecoin. — link
